name: pocketSQL
tagline: Steve Grubb's compact embeddable SQL engine for shell scripts and C programs (2001–2002); abandoned.
description: pocketSQL was a compact, multiuser SQL database by Steve Grubb (author of the Ploticus charting tool) designed to be linked straight into programs or driven from the shell rather than run as a server. It provided a simple C API, a command-line interface named psql (unrelated to PostgreSQL's), web access through his cgipal tool, a subset of SQL with SELECT INTO, joins, GROUP BY and ORDER BY, plus extensions to pipe results to shell commands and read ordinary files as tables, with file-level locking and transaction logging. It deliberately skipped indexing, logins and network access: processes had to share the data's file system and UID. The project dates from about 2001–2002 and its site is now a parked domain; use SQLite instead.
statusNote: Unmaintained since about 2002; the sgpr.net project page is now a parked domain. SQLite is the obvious replacement.

scale.notes: No indexes, so practical only for small tables.

strengths: Shell-friendly design: SQL results can pipe into commands and read plain files
Tiny library that links directly into C programs
weaknesses: No indexes, logins or network access
Abandoned around 2002 and hard to find today
useCases: Historical reference for script-oriented embedded SQL
Comparing early embedded SQL designs with SQLite
